How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
summary: VocabX is a vocabulary specialization method that reduces inference cost by 77% for domain-specific small language models like Qwen3-4B without retraining. Unlike existing approaches that optimize by token frequency, VocabX weights tokens by their actual cost—generated tokens cost 7.4x more than input tokens—and uses five specialized miners to identify repeated spans for macro tokens. Applied to a Portuguese essay grader, it reduced output tokens from 350 to 101 while improving quality scores from 0.703 to 0.810. The key insight: optimize for expensive tokens first, not total token count.

FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
summary: FairStress is a benchmark with 13+ million test cases measuring demographic fairness in LLM decision-making beyond final outputs, testing whether models equally resist changing correct decisions when challenged by adversarial arguments favoring different demographic groups. It matters because models used in hiring, lending, and healthcare often show "anti-stereotypical over-correction"—abandoning stronger candidates more readily when doing so favors minority-coded individuals. Key finding: frontier models like Claude Opus and GPT-4.5 switched toward minority candidates 8.8-42.4 percentage points more readily than majority candidates under matched persuasive arguments, revealing hidden asymmetries invisible in standard fairness benchmarks.

title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
summary: ALTK-Evolve uses learned memory—behavioral guidelines extracted from agent trajectories—to improve customer service agents without weight updates. A basic ReAct agent with GPT-4.1 reaches 67.5% Pass^4 on τ²-bench retail, topping the leaderboard and outperforming fine-tuned models like RAFT-30B-A3B (61.4%). Guidelines are automatically distilled from training attempts into rules appended to the system prompt, improving reliability (+10 points on Pass^4) while slightly reducing conversation length and latency. The approach works across models: GPT-4.1 agents gain +10 points on retail, while GPT-5.5 agents reach 82% Pass^4 on airline. Key takeaway: prompt-level memory beats fine-tuning for domain-specific agent improvement without model retraining.

Day-0 Support for Flint on vLLM
summary: vLLM now supports Recursive's Flint 40B MoE model from day one, with both NVFP4 and BF16 checkpoints running on a single GB200 GPU at ~500 tokens/s decode with 100K context. Flint activates only 2.5B of its 40B parameters per token using 256 experts and sliding-window attention across 35 layers, keeping full-context KV cache in just 14 layers. vLLM built custom kernels reducing decode latency 2.7× for NVFP4 by fusing operations, implementing small-batch MoE kernels, and using programmatic dependent launches. The key takeaway: specialized kernel optimization for model-specific architectures can dramatically improve serving efficiency even on modern hardware.

title: Announcing Humming: Fast, Flexible Kernels for Quantized Inference
summary: Ant Group and vLLM open-sourced Humming, a unified kernel library for quantized inference supporting NVIDIA GPUs from Turing onward and CUDA-compatible devices. It handles diverse quantization formats (W4A16, W8A8, W4A8, W4A4, MXFP4) through a composable architecture separating quantization representation from execution, with JIT compilation reducing kernel compilation from 23 seconds to under 2 seconds. Humming substantially outperforms Marlin, FlashInfer, and DeepGEMM across workloads—achieving 3-5× speedups on W4A16 at small batch sizes and 14-43% end-to-end throughput gains on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The key takeaway: unified quantization representation with device-specific tuning enables efficient support for multiple formats and architectures without duplicating kernel implementations.
